controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by Kepler-7; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured colour.
controls.notes: No image or colour of Kepler-7 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the colour of kepler-7's light, as its colour lens measures it.

controls.label: Illustration
controls.qualification: NASA's artist's concept of Kepler-7 b, from Eyes on Exoplanets; not an observation.
controls.notes: NASA's artist's concept of Kepler-7 b: the map its Eyes on Exoplanets app wraps around the planet. Nobody has resolved this planet's disc, so none of the colour, clouds or terrain in it was observed. Its longitudes are arbitrary.

charts.alt: The orbits of Kepler-7's planets in this map from above, to scale, with Kepler-7 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

Kepler-7 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (75, 80, 81) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 121660904, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 21-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.

physical.credit: Radius from Esteves et al. 2015 (2015ApJ...804..150E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; mass from Esteves et al. 2015, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2015ApJ...804..150E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; orbit from Esteves et al. 2015 (2015ApJ...804..150E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive
